For sure it's not the most critical problem, but say it's not a problem...

If user does not have possibility (or easy to access) to logout, he/she probably (in situation when need to leave fast for example) just closing a browser window/tab.

Which:

  * leaves session open on the server side - increases timewindow to take over session
  * if session hijacked, without logging out it leaves it usable for an attacker
  * leaves possibility if someone access same device/workstation, can continue using active session
  * (if there is no short server-side idle-timeout solution) then later it can be filled precondition for CSRF attacks

To undestand, that logout functionality itself is important, we have other requirements like:

  * V3.3.3 Verify that the application gives the option to terminate all other active sessions after a successful password change (including change via password reset/recovery), and that this is effective across the application, federated login (if present), and any relying parties.
  * V3.3.4 Verify that users are able to view and (having re-entered login credentials) log out of any or all currently active sessions and devices.


To be clear with that: there is no question, should we have logout functionality - we need to have. The question is (reason for this issue), should we have separate requirement, that this logout link/button must be available on every page.
